content.name: Aisha Rahman
content.title: Healthcare Assistant, GP Practice
content.summary: Healthcare assistant at a busy GP surgery, running phlebotomy, ECG and NHS Health Check clinics after starting out as a care assistant while finishing my BTEC. I am working towards the Level 3 Senior Healthcare Support Worker apprenticeship and speak Urdu and Bengali with many of our patients.

experience.title: Care Assistant (part-time)
bullets: Supported 12 residents per shift with personal care, mobility and meals in a 40-bed residential home, many living with dementia.
Recorded fluid charts and repositioning on the electronic care planning system and flagged changes to the senior carer.
Completed the Care Certificate within 10 weeks of starting.

experience.title: Healthcare Assistant
bullets: Run daily phlebotomy clinics of 25–30 patients for a practice of 11,500 registered patients, keeping haemolysed samples below 2%.
Carry out ECGs, blood pressure checks, height and weight and urine dipsticks, recording results in EMIS Web for GP review.
Deliver around 40 NHS Health Checks a month, giving lifestyle advice and booking follow-ups for patients with raised risk scores.
Helped the practice nurse give 1,300 flu vaccines during the 2025 autumn campaign under patient-specific directions.

education.degree: BTEC Level 3 National Extended Diploma in Health and Social Care, D*D*D
GCSEs: 8 at grades 9–5, including English Language (7), Maths (6) and Combined Science (6-6)
